title: Establish compliance-first onboarding lane with staged canary and automated eval heuristics for enterprise model requests
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers are requesting faster model catalog onboarding that guarantees compliance requirements (KMS/HSM, data residency, SSO/K8s RBAC) and predictable quality. Current intake is manual and ad-hoc, leading to long lead times and missed privacy/regulatory checks.

Proposal: Create a dedicated 'Compliance-first' intake lane for enterprise model requests that integrates automated heuristics (eval smoke tests, cost/latency profiling, quantization compatibility checks, PII detection) and a staged canary rollout path. The lane should produce a pass/fail gating decision and an actionable pinning/rejection recommendation.

Scope: New-model adds and version pin requests for customers requiring enterprise controls. Does NOT cover incident-driven rollback flows (tracked separately).

Stakeholders: PM (Maya Chen), Runtime Eng (Marco Alvarez), Infra (Priya Desai), Security & Compliance (Jen Park), Developer Experience (Nora Blake), Customer Success (Omar Reyes).
acceptance_criteria: Compliance lane intake form in Console that collects KMS/HSM, region/residency, data retention SLA, and customer compliance contact
Automated eval pipeline runs: functional smoke tests (subset of standard evals), latency/cost bench, and PII/skew checks within 2 hours for submitted model artifacts
Staged canary rollout orchestration: shadow -> 1% -> 10% -> 100% with automatic rollback triggers based on latency, error-rate, and quality regressions
Clear pin recommendation and deprecation window suggested by the pipeline when a new version is incompatible with customer constraints
Audit log entries and an exportable compliance report (PDF/CSV) attached to the catalog entry
Engineering sign-off on required runtime hooks and legal sign-off on compliance checklist
success_metrics: Mean time from enterprise request to catalog decision < 7 days (target)
>60% of enterprise model requests proceed through automated lane without manual legal review
Canary rollouts achieve successful gradation (1%->10%->100%) in >= 90% of cases without automated rollback
Number of compliance-related onboarding reverts reduced by 75% after launch
proposed_flow: 1) Customer submits enterprise model request via Console intake (new 'Compliance' lane). 2) Intake triggers automated evaluation pipeline: run smoke evals, cost/latency profile, quantization test, PII scan. 3) If all heuristics pass, create catalog entry with 'staged canary' flag. 4) Schedule canary rollout to customer traffic: shadow, 1%, 10%, full. 5) Monitor telemetry and quality signals; auto-rollback if thresholds breached. 6) On success, mark as 'enterprise-approved' and attach compliance report. 7) If heuristics fail, surface remediation steps and optional manual review.
implementation_notes: Pipeline to reuse existing eval harness with a curated enterprise prompt set (owned by PM + CS)
Runtime changes: add canary-traffic weighting, shadow mode, and automatic rollback hooks (ENG deliverable)
Console: new intake UI and 'compliance report' viewer (DX deliverable)
Security: integrate KMS/HSM check with onboarding metadata; ensure no sensitive keys are uploaded to platform
Telemetry: extend observability dashboards to show per-canary-stage metrics and quality regressions
risks: False positives from automated heuristics could slow down onboarding and frustrate customers
Insufficient coverage of proprietary customer prompts could allow regressions to slip through
Operational complexity in rollback automation might introduce customer-visible flaps if thresholds are too tight
Legal/regulatory variance across regions could require manual review despite automation
